what: Sherwin-Williams makes and sells paint and coatings. It runs about five thousand of its own stores selling mainly to professional painters, supplies retailers such as Lowe's, and sells industrial coatings for cars, packaging and machinery.
customers: Professional painting contractors above all, plus homeowners, carmakers, packaging producers and industrial manufacturers.
money: its own North American stores serving professional painters
paint sold through retailers and in Europe and Latin America
industrial, automotive and packaging coatings worldwide
moat: A store network that delivers to job sites the same day, which contractors rely on, and that no rival can build quickly.
risks: Housing turnover is weak, which reduces repainting demand
Growth has been slow at about 2% a year
Raw material costs, mainly petrochemicals, move with oil prices
Debt of about $14 billion after years of buybacks and acquisitions
opportunities: Pricing has held even when volumes fell, which protects margins
Professional contractors are a stickier customer base than do-it-yourself buyers
A recovery in housing transactions would lift repaint volumes
watch: Same-store sales in the Paint Stores Group, the core of its profit.
